ordered_diagnoses: Adnexal torsion of a parasitic fibroid
Ovarian cyst rupture with internal hemorrhage

s1.syndrome_frame: Acute abdominal pain in late pregnancy with vomiting and signs of peritoneal irritation
salient_findings: Acute left lower abdominal pain
Vomiting
Slight tenderness in the left abdomen without guarding initially, progressing to generalized tenderness with guarding
Presence of a left ovarian cyst with internal echoes and an avascular solid component
Rising CRP levels despite stable WCC
key_facts: 32-year-old primigravida at 36 weeks 3 days of gestation
Acute left lower abdominal pain
Vomiting
No vaginal bleeding, urinary symptoms, constipation, or changes in bowel habits
Stable observations and clinically well appearance
Slight tenderness in the left abdomen without guarding initially
Uterus was soft and relaxed
Foetal movements and monitoring were normal
Left ovarian cyst measuring 70 × 60 × 60 mm at 5 weeks
Cyst measured 63 × 33 × 69 mm with internal echoes and an avascular solid component at 32 weeks
Tumour markers (CEA, CA-19-9, CA-125) within normal limits
MDT review deemed the cyst benign and recommended surveillance
Hb was 121 g/L, WCC 10.0 × 10^9/L, neutrophils 9.1 × 10^9/L, platelets 270 × 10^9/L, and CRP 30 mg/L on admission
CRP rose to 209 mg/L over three days
WCC remained stable
Repeated transabdominal and transvaginal ultrasounds showed the left adnexal cyst unchanged in size and appearance

shortlist: Adnexal torsion of a parasitic fibroid

shortlist.label: Ovarian torsion
shortlist.why_kept: Acute abdominal pain and vomiting with signs of peritoneal irritation, consistent with ovarian torsion, especially given the history of a left ovarian cyst

shortlist.label: Ruptured ovarian cyst
shortlist.why_kept: Sudden onset of abdominal pain and rising inflammatory markers, which could indicate a ruptured ovarian cyst

shortlist.label: Appendicitis
shortlist.why_kept: Acute abdominal pain and vomiting, although the location of the pain is atypical for appendicitis

shortlist.label: Adnexal torsion of a parasitic fibroid
shortlist.why_kept: Similar presentation to ovarian torsion, and the patient has a history of a left ovarian cyst, which could be related to a parasitic fibroid

shortlist.label: Ovarian cyst rupture with internal hemorrhage
shortlist.why_kept: Severe abdominal pain and rising inflammatory markers, which could indicate internal hemorrhage due to a ruptured ovarian cyst

raw.rationale: The patient's acute left lower abdominal pain, vomiting, and rising inflammatory markers (CRP rose to 209 mg/L) are consistent with ovarian torsion, especially given the presence of a pre-existing ovarian cyst. The worsening pain and development of generalized tenderness with guarding in the left iliac fossa further support this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Ruptured ovarian cyst
rejected.why: The repeated ultrasounds showed the cyst unchanged in size and appearance, making rupture less likely

rejected.label: Appendicitis
rejected.why: The location of the pain and tenderness is in the left lower abdomen, which is atypical for appendicitis, and there are no urinary symptoms or changes in bowel habits

rejected.label: Adnexal torsion of a parasitic fibroid
rejected.why: There is no mention of a parasitic fibroid in the patient's history or imaging findings

rejected.label: Ovarian cyst rupture with internal hemorrhage
rejected.why: The ultrasounds did not show any evidence of free pelvic fluid or internal hemorrhage
